newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish pound slips below 89 pence, down vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Irish pound slips below 89 pence, down vs mark.

text.p: The Irish pound ran into selling pressure in morning trade on Thursday and was forced lower against both the mark and sterling, dealers said.
"The Irish pound is very offered this morning. There has been sizeable interest from the UK and continental Europe to sell it," one trader said.
By 0935 GMT, the punt was at 0.8865 sterling against 0.8935 at the open and 0.8954 at Wednesday's close after sterling rebounded against the mark on comments by UK Chancellor Gordon Brown.
Brown said in a Times interview that he had no plans for a special autumn budget to attempt to brake consumer spending.
Robust July housing figures also underpinned sterling by supporting the chances of a rate rise at next week's Bank of England meeting.
Meanwhile, the Irish pound dropped nearly one and a half pfennigs to 2.6718 marks from 2.6858 yesterday on the selling pressure.
But dealers said it should find a floor around 2.6650 marks and could ricochet back upwards as the weekend approaches.
The Irish pound has tended to move up against the mark on Fridays in recent weeks amid persistent market talk of a revaluation.
